name: Downward Dog
hero_alt: Downward-Facing Dog, seen from the side
meta_description: Rounded back, heels off the floor, bent elbows, sore wrists? Five things usually hold back Downward Dog, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
og_description: Five things usually hold back Downward Dog, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
lede: Hips high, back long, arms in line with your ears. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks seven things from the side. Here’s what good looks like.

rubric.name: Arms
rubric.good: In one line with your torso

fixes.outcome: your back will stay flat and your legs will straighten.
fixes.why: Tight hamstrings pull the pelvis under, round the back and keep the knees bent. Until they ease, bend your knees: a long back matters more than straight legs.
fixes.cue: Bend your knees and send your hips up and back.

fixes.outcome: your heels will reach closer to the floor.
fixes.why: Tight calves cap how far the ankle bends. Your heels don’t need to touch.
fixes.cue: Pedal your heels down toward the mat.

fixes.outcome: your arms will reach in one line with your torso.
fixes.why: Shoulder range runs out under load, so the arms stop short and the shoulders creep toward the ears.
fixes.cue: Reach your arms in line with your ears.

fixes.outcome: your arms will stay straight and your weight will shift back into your legs.
fixes.why: When the shoulders and core give way, the elbows bend and you lean forward into your hands.
fixes.cue: Push the floor away and send your hips back.

fixes.outcome: your weight will spread across the whole palm.
fixes.why: Weight sinking into the heel of the hand is the usual cause of wrist pain here.
fixes.cue: Spread your fingers and press through each knuckle.

cues: And one cue: let your head hang between your arms instead of looking forward.

faq.q: Do my heels need to touch the floor in Downward Dog?
faq.a: No. Lifted heels usually mean tight calves, not a mistake. Reach them toward the floor without forcing it.

faq.q: Is it OK to bend my knees in Downward Dog?
faq.a: Yes. If straight legs round your back, bend your knees. A long back matters more than straight legs.

faq.q: Why do my wrists hurt in Downward Dog?
faq.a: Usually too much weight in the heel of the hand. Spread your fingers, press through your knuckles, and send your hips back.

faq.q: How can I check my Downward Dog form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the side. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Downward Dog with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the five things that usually hold back Downward Dog (tight hamstrings, tight calves, stiff shoulders, weak pressing strength, stiff wrists), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
